quote: A Letter always feels to me like immortality because it is the mind alone without corporeal friend.
source: Emily Dickinson, Letters, L330, to Thomas Wentworth Higginson, June 1869 (ed. Thomas H. Johnson, 1958)

evidence.where: Dickinson Electronic Archives, Dickinson/Higginson correspondence, Letter 330 (Johnson numbering), read in context
evidence.edition: The Letters of Emily Dickinson, ed. Thomas H. Johnson and Theodora Ward (Harvard University Press, 1958)

reason: The sentence stands verbatim, with Dickinson's capital L on Letter, in the June 1869 letter to Higginson numbered 330 in Johnson. The same letter closes on Gratitude is the timid wealth of those who have nothing, so the month fit holds.
